title: Postmortem & Actions: "Pulse" noisy-tenant isolation, reservation miscalibration, and adaptive burst constraints
creator: Maya Chen
description: This ticket captures the postmortem, root cause analysis, and tracked remediation work after the 2026-03-09 dedicated cluster capacity event ("Pulse"). The event manifested as repeated eviction waves and large tail-latency spikes for multiple tenants due to a combination of a noisy tenant pattern, reservation sizing that didn't account for transient model memory spikes, and a permissive burst token policy that allowed sustained overcommit. The goal is to document temporary mitigations, define robust long-term fixes, and sequence actionable tasks for engineering and SRE teams.
incident_summary: 2026-03-09 02:20 UTC: Synthetic tenant-saturation monitors alerted. Between 02:18-02:55 UTC the dedicated-gpu-pool eu-west-01 experienced repeated eviction cycles and degraded 95th/99th token latencies. Multiple tenants reported 503s and high latencies; internal dashboards showed GPU memory pressure and KV-cache churn. The first mitigation (02:26 UTC) limited new burst grants globally; the second (03:10 UTC) applied a soft-fence to the largest noisy tenant. Normal service levels returned by 03:40 UTC. Impact affected ~8 active customers; two had reduced traffic and one experienced a visible outage to end-users.

root_cause: Root cause was multi-factor: (1) A noisy tenant (T-42) started a sustained multi-job workload with large sequence-length variance causing peak memory footprints beyond the reservation model; (2) reservations were sized using median working set estimates and did not include a burst hysteresis margin for transient model activations; (3) the burst token bucket policy permitted sustained replenishment across many small jobs, effectively permitting continuous overcommit for ~25 minutes; (4) KV cache eviction amplified pressure by increasing memory churn and triggering frequent kernel-level GC on the serving runtime. Collectively these produced eviction cascades and noisy-neighbor tail latency amplification.
mitigation_summary: During the incident we: (a) reduced global burst grant (fast config toggle) to slow new burst admissions, (b) soft-fenced tenant T-42 to its reservation and stopped its queued jobs from bursting, (c) drained and restarted a subset of overloaded worker pods to recover KV cache state, and (d) enabled extra telemetry (per-tenant KV churn, burst grant history) for post-incident analysis.
remediation_plan: - Implement reservation hysteresis: add a configurable buffer (default 20%) to avoid right-sized reservations from being saturated by transient peaks. Owner: Arjun Patel. Due: 2026-03-21.
- Add per-tenant burstDecay: ensure bursts decay over configurable windows (default 5m) so token bucket cannot be continuously refilled by short jobs. Owner: Priya Nair. Due: 2026-03-18.

- Create a noisy-tenant detection rule (synthetic + topology signals) that auto-tags tenants for review if sustained >X% of evictions originate from them for >10m. Owner: SRE team (Samir Gupta). Due: 2026-03-19.

- Fractional reservation accounting: prototype a fine-grained reservation allocator that supports fractional GPU crediting to reduce large-step rebalances. Owner: Runtime infra (Kenji Matsuda). Due: 2026-04-12.
- KV cache admission policy: add a hotspot throttle so that tenants causing persistent KV churn cannot evict other tenants' working sets. Owner: Serving runtime team (Lina Ortega). Due: 2026-04-05.
- Canary rollout: all changes to burst policy and reservation hysteresis must be canaried with tenant-synthetics and monitored for 72h. Owner: Release engineering. Due: 2026-04-15.

- Autoscaler heuristic update: include eviction-rate and KV-churn signals in autoscaler decisions to bias capacity growth for pools with persistent memory pressure. Owner: Autoscaler team. Due: 2026-06-01.
- Pricing/Quota refactor: ensure API/console exposes predicted tail-cost and recommends reservation sizing including hysteresis. Owner: Product + Developer Experience. Due: 2026-06-15.

decisions: 2) BurstDecay window = 5 minutes default; burst tokens must decay such that sustained bursts require proportionally larger reservation.
3) No global hard-eviction during canary; prefer soft-fence and throttles to retain predictable availability during rollout.
4) Prototype fractional reservations before large autoscaler changes to reduce blast radius.
